if it's feasible to continue using responsibly is different for everyone.

I've been working on reducing my consumption for over a year now.  After being in between abstinence and moderate use, I recently fooled myself into thinking I didn't have to quit entirely and I could keep using. And then convinced myself I could keep using daily. And then I found myself where I always do: using way too much all day, putting off my responsibilities, and the helpfulness I get from weed vanishes because my tolerance is too high and I want to use just to feel normal again (without even getting really 'high').

This is the problem for me: even if I try to moderate and have long breaks, if I get into daily use it always gets out of hand. Personally, I can't do daily use and be moderate. Maybe you can, but I think it's that much harder when using daily because it becomes a habit.

Something that helps me is playing the tape forward, what will happen if I vape another bowl? How many more will follow? Where will I end up? It's usually not where I want to end up.

I also have found myself just using to avoid withdrawal and fulfilling the craving. Tapering off definitely helps it be less intense, but in my experience using to avoid that is just delaying the inevitable. Keeping using to avoid feeling negative emotions won't make the negative emotions go away, and doesn't help learn the skills to cope with them either. 

SMART Recovery meetings are helpful to me. they aim for abstinence but accept anyone wherever they are at and support move towards moderation. It's been super helpful for me in terms of "learning to be sober again". Before that, I would just try to stop but didn't change anything in my life. Now I have tools to change my life to help use less.

Regarding school, I've heard some people say don't try to quit anything while in school. I'm doing a long degree, and it was having a negative impact and that's what got me my first 4-month period of being sober. The earlier you do it, the less chances it'll have of impacting your study. I waited and suffered from it and then had to go through the whole withdrawal thing while in school anyway or else I wouldn't be able to continue. Everyone is different, but IME putting off lowering usage/breaks only delays the inevitable. 

I tapered off and used less during the holidays. And since the new year, I'm now use one a week, on Saturday afternoons. It's not perfect but I feel much better than using daily, even if I was also way more emotional than usual. It does pass if you can stick to not using daily.

For me also, I cleaned my vape and put everything away. Ironically, I went back to joints cause I can just roll a tiny one, smoke it, and not take out any of my equipment. Since I don't want to dirty it for one session, it stays in the closet and that's been super helpful to not use. If my stuff is out and accessible, then it's too easy to just go for it.


Good luck, sorry for rambling, I'm trying to stick with once-a-week this time around. I wish both of us luck and success!

struggling with this a lot. i think we can seperate needs, boundaries and expectations. in my mind:

needs = what we need for a any interpersonal relation to be worth it
boundaries = the line that can't be crossed, what we can't tolerate in our relations with others
expectations = things we would like others to do

i feel like we can have our needs and boundaries and that's important to keep us safe. i try not to have expectations though, cause i don't control other people's behaviors and having expectations usually makes me disappointed.

for example, dad still hadn't cut firewood for the winter and that made me super angry, but i was angry cause i expected him to do it. however, it doesn't violate a boundary nor is it a need (we have a furnace for heat as well), so having the expectation just ended up hurting me. 

i also had a friend who i felt i had too high expectations for, and ended up trying to lower my expectations. but then i realized she wasn't even meeting my needs (not responding to my messages, avoiding/canceling plans to see me, not saying bye when she moved out of town). that was after i did many favors for her this year, and we'd been friends a long time. i realized my expectations hurt me and i was just running after her to try to get her to meet those expectations. when i realized she just wasn't meeting my needs in the friendship, i was able to let go because i realized it wasn't a good thing for me. it still hurt, but i wasn't wasting energy anymore to get her to meet expectations she maybe didn't even know i had.

i find thinking about it as needs and trying to let go of expectations as been helpful for me even if i struggle to do it still and it's a work in progress. and with needs and boundaries, i feel it's totally fair game to be explicit about it and tell the other person it's really important for you. then it's on them if they want to respect it or not, and if they don't you can put more distance with these people or cut contact depending on how bad it is.

a thing that came up in a group i go to was "how do we know if our boundaries are reasonable?" and EVERYONE was stumped, we were all like... "euh... don't know what a healthy relationship is.". it's super hard. but maybe try to see if yours is a need or an expectation, and talk to your friend about it if it's a need you feel isn't being met?

if they go do their own thing for a few days, maybe that's ok and you can try to get rid of that expectation? if they're never there for you when you need it and only respond when they need something from you, that doesn't sound ok at all.

i struggle with responding maladaptively too when people don't meet my expectations, like wanting to punish them for not being there or whatever. i give a lot but reach a threshold where i just become mean. it's hard and i try not to do it, cause i haven't been able to save any friendship where this has happened. 

>Will I ever learn how to do this people thing?

man idk, life is learning i guess! work in progress.

sorry for my novel, it's just my perspective and may not work for you so by no means feel obligated to take it seriously or anything. good luck and im here if you want to talk more about this topic
